verdicts.summary: The module-level queue keeps a prompt that arrives before the dialog mounts, and the dialog shows it once mounted. An already-expired prompt is marked passed as soon as the deadline store subscribes.
verdicts.scenario: Desktop sends ssh-1 while the renderer is on /pair or an unauthenticated page, so no SshPasswordPromptDialog is mounted (it renders only in the authenticated or hosted-static branch, __root.tsx:239). The bridge listener added at app start appends the prompt (SshPasswordPromptDialog.tsx:51-52). Later the shell mounts, useSyncExternalStore reads the queue (line 71), and the dialog renders the head. If the 3-minute main-process timeout (DesktopSshPasswordPrompts.ts:18) has passed, deadlineStore.subscribe sets passed = Date.now() >= deadline (clock.ts:130), so 'Expired' and Dismiss show. Dismiss and cancel remove only the head (line 67), and the next prompt then shows. Prompts the main process cancels without telling the renderer (window closed, service stopped) stay visible. That was true before too, while the dialog was mounted.

verdicts.summary: The new observer always runs before the _chat layout's window keydown listener. On /pull-requests, Escape therefore always leaves the page, and the sidebar thread selection is never cleared by Escape.
verdicts.scenario: 1. The shell mounts. SidebarControl's ref callback runs registerAppShellCommands during commit (AppSidebarLayout.tsx:341-343). The first registerCommands call installs the dispatcher's bubble listener on window (dispatcher.ts:88-92) before any passive effect runs. 2. ChatRouteGlobalShortcuts, a sibling of the PR Outlet (_chat.tsx:221), adds its window bubble listener in useEffect (_chat.tsx:175). It re-adds it whenever its deps change, so it always sits after the dispatcher. 3. The user is on /pull-requests and mod-clicks two sidebar threads (selectedThreadKeys.size = 2). 4. The user presses Escape. dispatchKeyDown runs first: no global scope handles Escape, so consumed = false. The observer (AppSidebarLayout.tsx:179-189) calls preventDefault and history.back(). 5. The _chat listener then returns early at _chat.tsx:72 because defaultPrevented is set, so _chat.tsx:88-90 (clear selection) never runs. In the old code, the PR page's listener was re-added on every page render (useNavigateBack returned a new closure each render, so the effect deps changed). Whichever listener was added last ran last, so Escape often cleared the selection first. The new ordering is fixed and always navigates. This also contradicts the new comment that a selection takes priority (AppSidebarLayout.tsx:173-174).
verdicts.consequence: With threads selected in the sidebar on the pull requests page, Escape leaves the page instead of clearing the selection, and the selection stays.

verdicts.summary: The probe always returns a promise, a rejection is swallowed, and the vscode fallback stays unless the probe returns a non-empty remote-capable list. The keepAlive atom runs the probe once.
verdicts.scenario: Tried three cases. (a) A non-desktop browser: probe is undefined, so the atom returns ['vscode']. (b) The IPC probe rejects: the rejection handler is a no-op, so the value stays ['vscode']. (c) The probe returns only editors that are not remote-capable: the filter result is empty, setSelf is not called, and ['vscode'] stays. The old code cached ['vscode'] in each of these cases, so the visible result is the same. A synchronous throw cannot happen because the preload wraps ipcRenderer.invoke (preload.ts:208).

verdicts.summary: The only open hazard is that shell atoms are mounted before authentication. Mounting them acquires environment supervisors through followStream (registry.ts:431-456, shell.ts:475-479) and can fire visit commands from cached shells. Finding 1 already raises this. The rest checks out: open-thread params match useParams(strict:false), the UI store hydrates synchronously from localStorage, and announcements made while no region is attached are dropped, as the note says.
